classification.habit: Moderate to large deciduous tree, up to 30 m high, with a straight clear bole.
classification.habitat: Mixed deciduous forests on hilly and undulating ground.
classification.distribution: Peninsular and Central India, extending to Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Odisha.

identification.description: Large deciduous tree with grey bark that exudes a red gum (kino) when cut; imparipinnate leaves of 5–7 leathery leaflets, yellow flowers and orbicular winged pods.
identification.whole_plant: Large deciduous tree with grey bark exuding red kino, imparipinnate leaves and yellow flowers.
identification.stem: Bole straight; bark grey, rough, exuding a blood-red gum (kino) when cut.
identification.leaf: Imparipinnate with 5–7 alternate, oblong, coriaceous leaflets with an emarginate tip.
identification.flower: Yellow, fragrant, papilionaceous, in large terminal panicles.
identification.fruit: Orbicular, flat, winged pod 2.5–5 cm across, usually one-seeded.
identification.seed: Single, reniform, enclosed in the centre of the winged pod.
identification.bark: Grey to dark brown, rough, exuding red kino on injury.
identification_points: Heartwood golden-yellowish brown with darker streaks
Water in contact turns yellow with blue fluorescence
Very hard, heavy wood with astringent taste
Tree exudes red kino; fruit a round winged pod

therapeutics.precautions: May potentiate antidiabetic drugs; monitor blood glucose. Strong astringency may cause constipation.
therapeutics.contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy without advice, and in Vata-predominant constipation.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The heartwood contains stilbenes and flavonoids (pterostilbene, marsupin, pterosupin, epicatechin), along with tannins and resin.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Pterocarpus marsupium is a well-known anti-diabetic herb that also purifies the blood and helps with skin issues.
recognized_uses: Prameha (traditionally as water stored in Vijayasar wooden tumblers)
modern_information.safety_notes: Generally well tolerated in traditional use; additive glucose lowering with antidiabetic medication is possible.
